title: Trying to paint kingfisher blue
storyboard: Film: overhead watercolour of a kingfisher, timelapse, plus palette close-up mixing blues; 2 takes

scenes.headline: Why you can't quite paint kingfisher blue
That blue isn't made by pigment.
Tiny spongy structures in the feathers scatter blue light
scenes.body: The orange underside is pigment. The blue back is structure.
scenes.source: Stavenga et al. 2011, J Exp Biol

scenes.headline: Paint what you see. Note what makes it.

caption:
Every paint set loses to this bird.

Kingfisher orange comes from pigment, but the blue comes from nanostructures inside the feather barbs that scatter blue light, which is why paint can only approximate it.

Source: Stavenga et al. 2011, Journal of Experimental Biology.  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Storyboard: art timelapse with a science payoff (structural colour) that explains why the painting can't match; all real kingfisher video, third species and medium.
